interpretation: Available RGB segmentation is not the bottleneck count: 157 masks passed the declared engineering checks, not correctness checks. The fixed camera-facing/normal/coverage rules yielded eligible center evidence only in 12 cases. This is coverage of this implementation, not proof that all remaining scenes contain no usable geometric evidence.
Every actual correction is single-axis center-only and conditional on source size. No z center or size coordinates were eligible. This run cannot establish a benefit from observed size adaptation.
Three axis-level opposing-plane pairs passed the looser individual-plane tests, but none passed the stronger paired size tests. No threshold is changed in response.

RGB one-sided containment makes a distinct float32 coordinate change in 7 of 160 cases; all main paired supports, acceptance and preconstraint boxes remain identical. The additional coordinate effect is small compared with total plane-driven center motion.

A lower combined geometry/prior/RGB objective does not imply lower RGB term: the tradeoff can worsen containment while improving surface residual. RGB and point-plane cues can conflict or be differently scaled; the diagnostic does not establish which cue is task-correct.

Zero size coverage and 7 RGB-coordinate differences sharply limit what a subsequent task result could support. Task precision and the conditional adaptation gate remain for independent post-seal evaluation. No further G revision is justified by these unlabeled counts alone.
